Welcome to the official documentation for filo studios! We are thrilled to have you here. At filo studios, we specialize in creating high-quality FiveM scripts designed to enhance your gaming experience and bring your server to life.

# Error: You lack the required entitlement (/docs/common_escrow/lack)



```
You lack the required entitlement to use filo_vehiclekeys
```

**What does this mean?**

Some of our scripts use escrow system, which means scripts are linked to your FiveM account (the account you used on Tebex).

In order to work, the script(s) must be run in a server which is using a server key created by the same FiveM account you used on Tebex. You can create a server key in [CFX Portal](https://portal.cfx.re/).

Once you've created a server key, add it to your server's `server.cfg` like this:

```
sv_licenseKey "licensekeyhere"
```

**The script is on my friend's FiveM account**

To transfer the script to another account, you can head to:

[CFX Portal](https://portal.cfx.re/) -> Purchased assets tab -> Transfer to another account

cfx.re only allow scripts to be transferred 1 time, so you won't be able to transfer the script again if you do this.


# Error: syntax error near <\1> (/docs/common_escrow/parsing)



### Error Example [#error-example]

```bash
[script:filo_vehiclekeys] Error parsing script @filo_vehiclekeys/server/sv-main.lua in resource filo_vehiclekeys: @filo_vehiclekeys/server/sv-main.lua:1: syntax error near '<\1>'
[    c-scripting-core] Failed to load script server/sv-main.lua.
```

### Solutions [#solutions]

* **You are using FileZilla and files have been corrupted during transfer** - try using an alternative FTP client such as [WinSCP](https://winscp.net/eng/index.php)
* You are transferring the folder to your server file by file — **you must upload the .zip file as-is** and then extract it **after** it has been transferred to your VPS
* Your server version is too old, the minimum version is 4752
  * You can download updated server artifacts [here](https://runtime.fivem.net/artifacts/fivem/build_server_windows/master/)
  * ...or check out the official [FiveM guide](https://docs.fivem.net/docs/server-manual/setting-up-a-server/)

```lua
Config.JobsAllowed = {
    "mechanic",
```

```lua
Config.JobsAllowed = nil
```

```lua
Config.RequiredItem = "vehicle_jack"
```

Set to `nil` to disable the inventory requirement.


# Exports (/docs/free_resources/filo_jack/exports)



## IsLifted [#islifted]

Checks whether a vehicle has been fully lifted.

### Client [#client]

```lua
local lifted = exports.filo_jack:IsLifted(vehicle)
```

Specify a side.

```lua
local lifted = exports.filo_jack:IsLifted(vehicle, "left")
```

### Parameters [#parameters]

| Name   | Type   | Description                      |
| ------ | ------ | -------------------------------- |
| entity | number | Vehicle entity                   |
| side   | string | `"left"` or `"right"` (optional) |

### Returns [#returns]

```lua
boolean
```


# filo_jack (/docs/free_resources/filo_jack)



A realistic **FiveM vehicle jack** that allows players to physically lift either side of a vehicle using floor jacks.

## Features [#features]

* Lift either the left or right side independently
* Realistic pump-by-pump animation
* Accurate vehicle roll geometry
* Automatic height compensation
* Support for jacking both sides simultaneously
* Export available for detecting lifted vehicles

## Requirements [#requirements]

* [ox\_lib](https://github.com/overextended/ox_lib)
* [community\_bridge](https://github.com/TheOrderFivem/community_bridge)

Continue with the installation guide to get started.


# Installation (/docs/free_resources/filo_jack/installation)



## 1. Install the resource [#1-install-the-resource]

Place the resource inside your server's resources folder.

```
resources/
    filo_jack/
```

## 2. Ensure the resource [#2-ensure-the-resource]

Add the following to your `server.cfg`.

```
ensure ox_lib

# ensure frameworkName [qbx_core/qb-core]

ensure community_bridge
ensure filo_jack
```

## 3. Install dependencies [#3-install-dependencies]

Required:

* [ox\_lib](https://github.com/overextended/ox_lib)
* [community\_bridge](https://github.com/TheOrderFivem/community_bridge)

## 4. Inventory Item [#4-inventory-item]

Create the following inventory item.

```
['vehicle_jack'] = {
    label = 'Vehicle Jack',
    weight = 500,
},
```

An item image is included inside:

```
INSTALL/item images/
```

## 5. Restart the server [#5-restart-the-server]

Once installed, restart your server.


# Usage (/docs/free_resources/filo_jack/usage)



Approach either side of a vehicle.

Available interactions include:

| Action              | Description                    |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| Attach Jack (Left)  | Place a jack on the left side  |
| Attach Jack (Right) | Place a jack on the right side |
| Pump Jack (Left)    | Raise the left side            |
| Pump Jack (Right)   | Raise the right side           |
| Detach Jack (Left)  | Remove the left jack           |
| Detach Jack (Right) | Remove the right jack          |

## Notes [#notes]

* Players must be close to the vehicle.
* Players must stand on the correct side.
* Both sides may be lifted independently.
* Removing one jack correctly preserves the remaining side.


# filo_slashtire (/docs/free_resources/filo_slashtire)



`filo_slashtire` allows players to puncture vehicle tires using configurable melee weapons. The resource automatically detects the nearest tire, synchronizes the damage across all clients, and integrates with **ox\_target** for seamless interaction.

## Features [#features]

* Lightweight and optimized
* Automatic closest tire detection
* Configurable allowed weapons
* Fully synchronized tire damage
* Framework independent

## Requirements [#requirements]

* [ox\_lib](https://github.com/overextended/ox_lib)
* [ox\_target](https://github.com/overextended/ox_target)

## Installation [#installation]

1. Place `filo_slashtire` in your `resources` folder.
2. Ensure the required dependencies before the resource.

```
ensure ox_lib
ensure ox_target
ensure filo_slashtire
```

## Configuration [#configuration]

### Allowed Weapons [#allowed-weapons]

Configure which weapons can slash tires in:

```text
shared/sh-config.lua
```

Example:

```lua
Config.AllowedWeapons = {
    `WEAPON_KNIFE`,
    `WEAPON_SWITCHBLADE`,
    `WEAPON_DAGGER`
}
```

Any GTA V weapon hash can be added or removed from this table.

## Usage [#usage]

1. Equip one of the configured weapons.
2. Walk up to a vehicle tire.
3. Target the tire using **ox\_target**.
4. Select **Slash Tire**.
5. The tire will be punctured for everyone on the server.

## Compatibility [#compatibility]

| Resource   | Required |
| ---------- | -------- |
| ox\_lib    | ✅        |
| ox\_target | ✅        |

## Support [#support]

If you encounter an issue, please include:

* Server artifacts version
* Resource version
* Console errors
* Steps to reproduce

For support and updates:

* **Discord**: [https://discord.gg/ReEE9HgA4c](https://discord.gg/ReEE9HgA4c)
* **Store**: [https://filo.tebex.io](https://filo.tebex.io)

```
```


# Configuration (/docs/free_resources/filo_bolt/configuration)





## config.lua [#configlua]

All static options live in `config.lua` at the root of the resource. Changes take effect on the next resource restart.

```lua title="config.lua"
Config = {}

-- RGBA colour applied to the draw-outline on a hovered bolt.
-- Values: 0–255 per channel.
Config.OutlineColor = { r = 255, g = 255, b = 255, a = 255 }

-- When true, the player must wait for the current bolt to finish
-- rotating before they can click another one.
Config.OneAtATime = false
```

## Options [#options]

<TypeTable
  type="{
  OutlineColor: {
    description: &#x22;RGBA table controlling the colour of the bolt hover outline.&#x22;,
    type: &#x22;{ r: number, g: number, b: number, a: number }&#x22;,
    default: &#x22;{ r = 255, g = 255, b = 255, a = 255 }&#x22;,
  },
  OneAtATime: {
    description: &#x22;Restricts the player to animating one bolt at a time. Useful for slower, more deliberate gameplay.&#x22;,
    type: &#x22;boolean&#x22;,
    default: &#x22;false&#x22;,
  },
}"
/>

## Notes [#notes]

* `OutlineColor` uses the same RGBA range (0–255) as `SetEntityDrawOutlineColor`.
* `OneAtATime` only blocks the *start* of a new rotation — it does not cancel an animation already in progress.


# Examples (/docs/free_resources/filo_bolt/examples)





## Loosen a wheel [#loosen-a-wheel]

The most common use case — called before removing a tyre or wheel.

```lua
CreateThread(function()
    local vehicle = GetVehiclePedIsIn(cache.ped, false)
    if not DoesEntityExist(vehicle) then return end

    local success = exports.filo_bolt:Start({
        vehicle      = vehicle,
        wheelBone    = "wheel_lf",
        lugnutCount  = 5,
        isTightening = false,
    })

    if success then
        -- all bolts removed, proceed with wheel removal
    end
end)
```

***

## Tighten after fitting a wheel [#tighten-after-fitting-a-wheel]

Called after a new wheel has been attached. `canCancel = false` forces the player to complete the task.

```lua
CreateThread(function()
    local vehicle = GetVehiclePedIsIn(cache.ped, false)

    local success = exports.filo_bolt:Start({
        vehicle      = vehicle,
        wheelBone    = "wheel_rr",
        lugnutCount  = 6,
        isTightening = true,
        canCancel    = false,
    })

    if success then
        -- wheel secured
    end
end)
```

***

## Passing a bone index [#passing-a-bone-index]

If your resource works with bone indices rather than names, pass the index directly — `filo_bolt` resolves it internally.

```lua
local boneIdx = GetEntityBoneIndexByName(vehicle, "wheel_lr")

local success = exports.filo_bolt:Start({
    vehicle   = vehicle,
    wheelBone = boneIdx,
})
```

***

## Checking the result in a job flow [#checking-the-result-in-a-job-flow]

`Start` returns a plain boolean, so it fits cleanly into any sequential job logic.

```lua
CreateThread(function()
    local vehicle = GetVehiclePedIsIn(cache.ped, false)

    local wheels = { "wheel_lf", "wheel_rf", "wheel_lr", "wheel_rr" }

    for _, bone in ipairs(wheels) do
        local ok = exports.filo_bolt:Start({
            vehicle      = vehicle,
            wheelBone    = bone,
            lugnutCount  = 5,
            isTightening = false,
        })

        if not ok then
            -- player cancelled mid-job
            return
        end
    end

    -- all four wheels loosened
end)
```

<Callout type="warn">
  Always call `Start` inside a `CreateThread`. It blocks via `Citizen.Await` and will freeze your script if called outside a thread.
</Callout>


# Export (/docs/free_resources/filo_bolt/export)





## Start [#start]

Starts the bolt minigame for a specific vehicle wheel. The call **blocks** until the player either rotates all bolts or cancels.

```lua
local success = exports.filo_bolt:Start(data)
```

### Parameters [#parameters]

`data` is a table with the following fields:

<TypeTable
  type="{
  vehicle: {
    description: &#x22;Entity handle of the vehicle the wheel belongs to.&#x22;,
    type: &#x22;integer&#x22;,
    required: true,
  },
  wheelBone: {
    description: 'Bone name (&#x22;wheel_lf&#x22;, &#x22;wheel_rf&#x22;, &#x22;wheel_lr&#x22;, &#x22;wheel_rr&#x22;) or a numeric bone index. If a bone index is passed it will be resolved to the matching name automatically.',
    type: &#x22;string | integer&#x22;,
    required: true,
  },
  lugnutCount: {
    description: &#x22;How many bolt entities to spawn around the wheel.&#x22;,
    type: &#x22;integer&#x22;,
    default: &#x22;5&#x22;,
  },
  isTightening: {
    description: &#x22;Direction of rotation. true rotates clockwise (tighten) and locks the bolt on completion. false rotates counter-clockwise (loosen) and enables physics so the bolt falls away.&#x22;,
    type: &#x22;boolean&#x22;,
    default: &#x22;false&#x22;,
  },
  canCancel: {
    description: &#x22;Whether the player can exit the minigame early by pressing Escape or Backspace.&#x22;,
    type: &#x22;boolean&#x22;,
    default: &#x22;true&#x22;,
  },
}"
/>

### Return value [#return-value]

| Value   | Meaning                               |
| ------- | ------------------------------------- |
| `true`  | All bolts were successfully rotated   |
| `false` | The player cancelled before finishing |

### Valid wheel bones [#valid-wheel-bones]

| Bone name  | Position    |
| ---------- | ----------- |
| `wheel_lf` | Front-left  |
| `wheel_rf` | Front-right |
| `wheel_lr` | Rear-left   |
| `wheel_rr` | Rear-right  |

<Callout>
  `Start` uses `Citizen.Await` internally. Call it inside a `CreateThread` — do not call it at the top level of a script or inside an event handler without a thread wrapper.
</Callout>

### Input bindings (while active) [#input-bindings-while-active]

| Input                  | Action                                               |
| ---------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| **Left Mouse Button**  | Rotate the hovered bolt                              |
| **Escape / Backspace** | Cancel and return `false` (if `canCancel` is `true`) |


# filo_bolt (/docs/free_resources/filo_bolt)



`filo_bolt` is a standalone FiveM resource that renders physical lug nut entities on a vehicle wheel and lets players interact with each one individually using a 3D cursor.

It is designed to slot into any mechanic, tyre, or vehicle repair workflow via a single blocking export — no framework coupling, no NUI overhead.

## How it works [#how-it-works]

When `Start()` is called, the resource:

1. Spawns bolt entities evenly distributed around the target wheel bone
2. Locks input and enables the mouse cursor
3. Raycasts from the cursor each frame to detect which bolt is hovered
4. On click, animates the bolt rotating around its Y-axis
5. Resolves the promise once all bolts are rotated (or the player cancels)
6. Cleans up all entities and restores the camera

Bolts that are loosened detach and fall with physics. Bolts that are tightened lock in place.

## Dependencies [#dependencies]

* [`ox_lib`](https://github.com/overextended/ox_lib) — required for `cache.ped`
* No framework (ESX / QBCore / etc.) required

## File structure [#file-structure]

```
filo_bolt/
├── client/
│   ├── cl-init.lua       -- Global constants
│   ├── cl-camera.lua     -- Scripted camera
│   ├── cl-bolt.lua       -- Bolt spawning, animation, cleanup
│   ├── cl-raycast.lua    -- Cursor raycast utility
│   ├── cl-sound.lua      -- Audio bank + playback
│   └── cl-main.lua       -- Orchestration + export
├── config.lua
└── fxmanifest.lua
```


# Installation (/docs/free_resources/filo_bolt/installation)





## Requirements [#requirements]

Before installing, make sure the following resource is running on your server:

* [`ox_lib`](https://github.com/overextended/ox_lib) — must be started before `filo_bolt`

## Steps [#steps]

<Steps>
  ### Download the resource [#download-the-resource]

  Purchase and download `filo_bolt` from [filo.tebex.io](https://filo.tebex.io). Extract the archive — you should have a single folder named `filo_bolt`.

  ### Add to your resources [#add-to-your-resources]

  Move the `filo_bolt` folder into your server's `resources` directory (or whichever sub-folder you organise resources into).

  ```
  resources/
  └── [filo]/
      └── filo_bolt/
  ```

  ### Add the audio bank [#add-the-audio-bank]

  Place the custom audio files at the following path inside the resource:

  ```
  filo_bolt/audiodirectory/filo_bolt_sounds.awc
  ```

  This file is included in the download. The resource will not throw an error if it is missing, but bolt sounds will not play.

  ### Ensure in server.cfg [#ensure-in-servercfg]

  Add the following line to your `server.cfg`, **after** `ox_lib`:

  ```
  ensure ox_lib
  ensure filo_bolt
  ```

  ### Restart or start the resource [#restart-or-start-the-resource]

  ```
  start filo_bolt
  ```
</Steps>

<Callout type="warn">
  Do not rename the resource folder. The export is registered under `filo_bolt` and callers reference it by that name.
</Callout>


# Configuration (/docs/free_resources/filo_stealwheels/configuration)



Configuration is located in:

```
shared/sh-config.lua
```

## Wheel Item [#wheel-item]

```lua
Config.WheelItem = "vehicle_wheel"
```

Inventory item received after removing a wheel.

***

## Filo Jack Integration [#filo-jack-integration]

```lua
Config.UseFiloJack = true
```

When enabled, players must lift vehicles using **Filo Jack** before wheels can be removed.

Disable if you don't use Filo Jack.

```lua
Config.UseFiloJack = false
```

***

## Filo Bolt Integration [#filo-bolt-integration]

```lua
Config.UseFiloBolt = true
```

When enabled, players must remove bolts using **Filo Bolt** before wheels can be removed.

Disable if you don't use Filo Bolt.

```lua
Config.UseFiloBolt = false
```

***

## Required Tool [#required-tool]

```lua
Config.RequiredItem = "tire_iron"
```

Tool required for wheel removal.

Set to `nil` to disable.

```lua
Config.RequiredItem = nil
```

***

## Item Durability [#item-durability]

```lua
Config.DecreaseDurability = {
    enabled = true,
    amount = 10
}
```

Decrease the durability of the tire iron after each use.

* `enabled` enables durability loss.
* `amount` specifies how much durability is removed.


# FAQ (/docs/free_resources/filo_stealwheels/faq)



## I can't remove wheels. [#i-cant-remove-wheels]

Make sure:

* You have a tire iron.
* The vehicle is accessible.
* If Filo Jack integration is enabled, the vehicle is lifted.

***

## Can I use this without Filo Jack? [#can-i-use-this-without-filo-jack]

Yes.

Set:

```lua
Config.UseFiloJack = false
```

***

## Can I disable the required item? [#can-i-disable-the-required-item]

Yes.

```lua
Config.RequiredItem = nil
```

***

## Can I disable durability loss? [#can-i-disable-durability-loss]

Yes.

```lua
Config.DecreaseDurability.enabled = false
```


# filo_stealwheels (/docs/free_resources/filo_stealwheels)



Filo Steal Wheels allows players to remove wheels from vehicles using a tire iron. The script features realistic wheel removal, optional integration with &#x2A;*[filo\_jack](https://filo.tebex.io/package/filo-jack)**, and ox\_inventory support.

## Features [#features]

* Remove individual vehicle wheels
* Install removed wheels back onto vehicles
* Compatible with ox\_inventory
* Optional [filo\_jack](https://filo.tebex.io/package/filo-jack) integration
* Configurable required items
* Configurable durability loss
* Lightweight and optimized

## Requirements [#requirements]

* [ox\_lib](https://github.com/overextended/ox_lib)
* [ox\_inventory](https://github.com/overextended/ox_inventory)
* [community\_bridge](https://github.com/TheOrderFivem/community_bridge)

> **Optional**
>
> * [filo\_jack](https://filo.tebex.io/package/filo-jack)
> * [filo\_bolt](https://filo.tebex.io/package/filo-bolt)


# Installation (/docs/free_resources/filo_stealwheels/installation)



## 1. Install the resource [#1-install-the-resource]

Copy the resource into your server's resources folder.

```
resources/
    filo_stealwheels/
```

## 2. Add to server.cfg [#2-add-to-servercfg]

```
ensure filo_stealwheels
```

## 3. Install dependencies [#3-install-dependencies]

Required:

* [ox\_lib](https://github.com/overextended/ox_lib)
* [ox\_inventory](https://github.com/overextended/ox_inventory)
* [community\_bridge](https://github.com/TheOrderFivem/community_bridge)

Optional:

* [filo\_jack](https://filo.tebex.io/package/filo-jack)
* [filo\_bolt](https://filo.tebex.io/package/filo-bolt)

## 4. Import inventory items [#4-import-inventory-items]

The package includes an example item configuration.

```
INSTALL/ox_inventory.txt
```

Also import the provided item images.

```
INSTALL/item images/
```

Images included:

* tire\_iron.png
* vehicle\_wheel.png

## 5. Restart your server [#5-restart-your-server]

Restart the server after installation.


# Usage (/docs/free_resources/filo_stealwheels/usage)



## Removing Wheels [#removing-wheels]

1. Approach a vehicle.
2. (Optional) Lift the vehicle using **Filo Jack**.
3. Use a tire iron.
4. Select the wheel to remove.
5. The removed wheel is added to the player's inventory.

## Notes [#notes]

* Wheels are handled individually.
* Filo Jack integration is optional.
* Tire iron durability can decrease after every use.


# DrawText3D (/docs/free_resources/filo_textui/draw-text-3d)





Spawns a DUI-backed label rendered as a billboard in the game world. Each call from a resource manages a single label — calling `DrawText3D` again from the same resource will **update** the existing label rather than spawn a new one.

## Signature [#signature]

```lua
exports.filo_textui:DrawText3D(data)
```

## Parameters [#parameters]

| Field          | Type      | Required | Description                                                  |
| -------------- | --------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `entity`       | `number`  | —        | Entity handle to attach the label to.                        |
| `coords`       | `vector3` | —        | World position for a static (non-entity) label.              |
| `options`      | `table`   | ✓        | Array of label entries. See [Options](#options).             |
| `distance`     | `number`  | —        | Visibility range in units. Default: `8.0`.                   |
| `entityOffset` | `vector3` | —        | Override the automatic anchor offset relative to the entity. |

<Callout type="warning">
  Either `entity` or `coords` must be provided.
</Callout>

### Options [#options]

Each entry in the `options` array:

| Field   | Type     | Required | Description                                              |
| ------- | -------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `key`   | `string` | —        | Key badge character. Supported: `E`, `F`, `G`, `H`, `X`. |
| `label` | `string` | ✓        | Display text. Rendered uppercase.                        |

Omitting `key` renders a plain text pill with no badge.

## Auto anchor offsets [#auto-anchor-offsets]

When `entityOffset` is not provided, the anchor is calculated from the entity's bounding box:

| Entity type | Anchor offset                    |
| ----------- | -------------------------------- |
| Ped         | `vector3(maxX + 0.35, 0.0, 0.0)` |
| Vehicle     | `vector3(maxX + 0.55, 0.0, 0.3)` |

## Examples [#examples]

### Attached to an entity [#attached-to-an-entity]

```lua
exports.filo_textui:DrawText3D({
    entity  = entityId,
    options = {
        { key = 'E', label = 'Interact' },
        { key = 'G', label = 'Options' },
    },
})
```

### Multiple labels, one without a key [#multiple-labels-one-without-a-key]

```lua
exports.filo_textui:DrawText3D({
    entity  = entityId,
    options = {
        { key = 'E', label = 'Enter Vehicle' },
        { label = 'Locked' },
    },
})
```

### Fixed world coordinates [#fixed-world-coordinates]

```lua
exports.filo_textui:DrawText3D({
    coords   = vector3(100.0, 200.0, 30.0),
    distance = 5.0,
    options  = {
        { key = 'E', label = 'Open' },
    },
})
```

### Custom anchor offset [#custom-anchor-offset]

```lua
exports.filo_textui:DrawText3D({
    entity       = entityId,
    entityOffset = vector3(0.0, 0.0, 1.5),
    options      = {
        { key = 'F', label = 'Fuel' },
    },
})
```

### Updating an existing label [#updating-an-existing-label]

Calling `DrawText3D` from the same resource again will patch the label in-place:

```lua
-- Initial show
exports.filo_textui:DrawText3D({
    entity  = entityId,
    options = { { key = 'E', label = 'Lock' } },
})

-- Later — updates without spawning a new DUI
exports.filo_textui:DrawText3D({
    entity  = entityId,
    options = { { key = 'E', label = 'Unlock' } },
})
```


# DrawText (/docs/free_resources/filo_textui/draw-text)





Shows a screen-space prompt bar anchored to the bottom center of the screen. Accepts a table of options, a plain string, or a shorthand entity form. Calling `DrawText` again with identical options is a no-op.

## Signature [#signature]

```lua
exports.filo_textui:DrawText(options)
exports.filo_textui:DrawText(string)
exports.filo_textui:DrawText(string, { entity = entityId })
```

## Parameters [#parameters]

### Table form [#table-form]

```lua
exports.filo_textui:DrawText({
    options = {
        { key = 'E', label = 'Engine' },
        { key = 'G', label = 'Gear' },
    }
})
```

| Field     | Type    | Required | Description             |
| --------- | ------- | -------- | ----------------------- |
| `options` | `table` | ✓        | Array of label entries. |

### Options [#options]

| Field   | Type     | Required | Description                                              |
| ------- | -------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `key`   | `string` | —        | Key badge character. Supported: `E`, `F`, `G`, `H`, `X`. |
| `label` | `string` | ✓        | Display text. Rendered uppercase.                        |

### String shorthand [#string-shorthand]

The key is parsed from square brackets in the string. Everything outside the brackets becomes the label.

```lua
exports.filo_textui:DrawText('[E] Interact')
```

### Entity shorthand [#entity-shorthand]

Passing a second argument with an `entity` field delegates to [`DrawText3D`](/filo_textui/draw-text-3d) instead of showing the bottom bar.

```lua
exports.filo_textui:DrawText('[E] Interact', { entity = entityId })
```

<Callout type="info">
  The entity shorthand is a convenience wrapper. It creates a single-row 3D label on the given entity — identical to calling `DrawText3D` directly.
</Callout>

## Examples [#examples]

### Multiple prompts [#multiple-prompts]

```lua
exports.filo_textui:DrawText({
    options = {
        { key = 'E', label = 'Enter' },
        { key = 'F', label = 'Flip' },
        { label = 'Stolen' },
    }
})
```

### String shorthand [#string-shorthand-1]

```lua
exports.filo_textui:DrawText('[E] Open Door')
```

### Updating the bar [#updating-the-bar]

Call `DrawText` again with different options to swap the prompts. If the options are identical to what's already showing, the call is ignored.

```lua
exports.filo_textui:DrawText({ options = { { key = 'E', label = 'Lock' } } })

-- swap later
exports.filo_textui:DrawText({ options = { { key = 'E', label = 'Unlock' } } })
```


# HideText3D (/docs/free_resources/filo_textui/hide-text-3d)



Removes the DUI and cleans up the render thread for a 3D label. Safe to call even if the label is not currently visible.

## Signature [#signature]

```lua
exports.filo_textui:HideText3D()
```

No arguments are required. The label owned by the calling resource is destroyed.

## Example [#example]

```lua
exports.filo_textui:DrawText3D({
    entity  = entityId,
    options = { { key = 'E', label = 'Interact' } },
})

-- Later, when the interaction zone is left
exports.filo_textui:HideText3D()
```


# HideText (/docs/free_resources/filo_textui/hide-text)



Hides the bottom bar and stops the key-press polling thread.

## Signature [#signature]

```lua
exports.filo_textui:HideText()
```

## Example [#example]

```lua
local insideZone = false

-- On zone enter
exports.filo_textui:DrawText({ options = { { key = 'E', label = 'Interact' } } })
insideZone = true

-- On zone exit
if insideZone then
    exports.filo_textui:HideText()
    insideZone = false
end
```


# filo_textui (/docs/free_resources/filo_textui)





A lightweight text UI library for FiveM. Render interactive key prompts attached to entities or world coordinates, or display a contextual bottom bar — both with live key-press feedback.

## Display modes [#display-modes]

**3D world labels** are rendered directly in the game world as billboarded DUI textures. They scale with distance, auto-orient to the entity's forward vector, and clean up automatically when the tracked entity is removed.

**2D bottom bar** is a screen-space prompt bar anchored to the bottom center of the screen. It slides in on show and supports the same key badge system.

Both modes support optional key badges (`E` `F` `G` `H` `X`) that visually highlight when the player holds the corresponding key, making them well suited for interaction prompts.

## Dependencies [#dependencies]

* [`ox_lib`](https://github.com/overextended/ox_lib)

## Installation [#installation]

1. Drop `filo_textui` into your resources folder.
2. Add `ensure filo_textui` to your `server.cfg` **before** any resource that uses it.

<Callout type="info">
  `filo_textui` must start before any resource that calls its exports.
</Callout>

## Configuration [#configuration]

```lua title="config.lua"
Config.FollowCamera = false
```

| Option         | Type      | Default | Description                                                                                 |
| -------------- | --------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `FollowCamera` | `boolean` | `false` | When `true`, labels on entities rotate their anchor to always face the camera horizontally. |


# IsTextVisible (/docs/free_resources/filo_textui/is-text-visible)



Returns `true` if a 3D label spawned by the calling resource is currently active.

## Signature [#signature]

```lua
local visible = exports.filo_textui:IsTextVisible()
```

## Returns [#returns]

| Type      | Description                                     |
| --------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `boolean` | `true` if a label is active, `false` otherwise. |

## Example [#example]

```lua
if not exports.filo_textui:IsTextVisible() then
    exports.filo_textui:DrawText3D({
        entity  = entityId,
        options = { { key = 'E', label = 'Interact' } },
    })
end
```


# Changelog (/docs/paid_resources/filo_vehiclekeys/changelog)





## 2.0.0 [#200]

**Added**

* NPC carjacking: aim at a driver, hold them up, take the car and its key
* Vehicle class difficulty tiers with per-class lockpick/hotwire chances and hotwire times
* Model blacklist for lockpicking, hotwiring and carjacking
* Police bypass (job, grade, duty and optional `police_bypass` item)
* Dispatch alerts: ps-dispatch, built-in notify + blip, or your own function
* tr\_minigames physical lockpick and hotwire (included, pre-configured)
* sleepless\_prompts for all prompts (included, replaces filo\_textui)
* `/keyadmin` panel to manage vehicles, key IDs, job access and keys
* Automatic key removal for unowned vehicles on despawn and restart
* `HasVehicleAccess` export (client and server)

**Changed**

* Reworked key system: one server-side registry, key IDs validated on the server
* Framework, inventory, minigames, dispatch and target code moved to an open `bridge/` folder
* Admin command is now `/keyadmin`

**Fixed**

* `/givekey` with plates containing spaces and stored vehicles
* Locksmith keys not saving, double key removal and many other bugs
* Exploits: lock/unlock without keys, client-set state bags, spare key pricing

## Updating from v1 [#updating-from-v1]

<Steps>
  <Step>
    Replace the 

    `filo_vehiclekeys`

     folder. Back up your 

    `shared/sh-config.lua`

     first: the config has new sections, so copy your values over instead of reusing the old file.
  </Step>

  <Step>
    Add 

    `sleepless_prompts`

    , 

    `tr_core`

     and 

    `tr_minigames`

     from the download. 

    `filo_textui`

     is no longer needed.
  </Step>

  <Step>
    Add 

    `police_bypass`

     from 

    `filo_vehiclekeys/INSTALL/ox_inventory.txt`

     and 

    `wire_strippers`

     from 

    `tr_minigames/install/ox_inventory/items.lua`

    .
  </Step>

  <Step>
    Ensure them in this order:

    ```
    ensure sleepless_prompts
    ensure filo_vehiclekeys
    ensure tr_core
    ensure tr_minigames
    ```
  </Step>
</Steps>

<Callout type="info">
  Existing key data in the `filo_vehiclekeys` table is kept. Scripts using the v1
  `filo_vehiclekey` exports keep working through the compatibility layer.
</Callout>


# Compatibility (/docs/paid_resources/filo_vehiclekeys/compatibility)





## qb-vehiclekeys & qbx\_vehiclekeys [#qb-vehiclekeys--qbx_vehiclekeys]

`filo_vehiclekeys` provides `qb-vehiclekeys`, `qbx_vehiclekeys` and `filo_vehiclekey` (v1), so
garages and job scripts that use them keep working without changes.

```lua
-- qb-vehiclekeys
TriggerServerEvent('qb-vehiclekeys:server:AcquireVehicleKeys', plate)
TriggerEvent('vehiclekeys:client:SetOwner', plate)

-- qbx_vehiclekeys
lib.callback.await('qbx_vehiclekeys:server:giveKeys', false, netId)
exports.qbx_vehiclekeys:GiveKeys(source, vehicle)
exports.qbx_vehiclekeys:RemoveKeys(source, vehicle)
exports.qbx_vehiclekeys:SetLockState(vehicle, state)
exports.qbx_vehiclekeys:HasKeys(vehicle) -- client
```

## tr\_minigames [#tr_minigames]

Set `Config.Minigames = 'tr_minigames'` to use tr\_minigames' physical lockpick and hotwire.
filo\_vehiclekeys stays in charge of input and prompts; tr\_minigames runs the minigame and decides
the outcome.

* **Hotwire:** the hotwire key (`H`) and prompt start tr\_minigames' hotwire. The prompt only shows when you have no key and carry `Config.TrMinigames.HotwireItem`.
* **Lockpick:** using the `lockpick` item starts tr\_minigames' lockpick. A successful pick unlocks the car.
* **After a hotwire:** the car is marked hotwired and runs without a key being handed out.
* **Access checks:** tr\_minigames asks filo\_vehiclekeys through `HasVehicleAccess`. Keys, job keys and the police bypass all count.

The `tr_core` and `tr_minigames` folders in the download are pre-configured (`keys = 'filo_vehiclekeys'`,
their own prompts, target option and keybinds off). Ensure them **after** `filo_vehiclekeys`:

```
ensure filo_vehiclekeys
ensure tr_core
ensure tr_minigames
```

<Callout type="warn">
  In this mode, difficulty, class tiers, alarms and lockpick/hotwire alerts come from tr\_minigames'
  own config. `Config.Blacklist` is still checked before a hotwire starts, but copy the models into
  tr\_minigames' `excludeModels` too. Keep `Config.TrMinigames.HotwireItem` equal to tr\_minigames'
  `Config.hotwire.item` (default `wire_strippers`).
</Callout>

## Editing the bridge [#editing-the-bridge]

Everything that depends on another resource lives in `bridge/` and stays open when escrowed.

| File                                             | What it contains                                                                |
| ------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `bridge/framework/client.lua` / `server.lua`     | Player job, money, owned vehicles, usable items, vehicle names                  |
| `bridge/inventory/client.lua` / `server.lua`     | Item checks, adding/removing items, durability, inventory reads                 |
| `bridge/minigames/client.lua`                    | Hotwire, lockpick, search and wiring minigames (each returns true on pass)      |
| `bridge/minigames/server.lua`                    | Syncs results from tr\_minigames into the key state                             |
| `bridge/dispatch/client.lua`                     | ps-dispatch, builtin and custom dispatch                                        |
| `bridge/target/client.lua`                       | Lock/unlock target options on vehicles                                          |
| `bridge/compatibility/client.lua` / `server.lua` | qb/qbx shims, plus `HasVehicleAccess` and `StartEngineWithoutKeys` for tr\_core |

To support another framework or inventory, change the function bodies and keep the function
names: the rest of the resource calls them by name.

<Callout type="info">
  Something broken after a third-party update? Open a ticket in the
  [Discord](https://discord.gg/EWKWXVBHK7).
</Callout>


# Configuration (/docs/paid_resources/filo_vehiclekeys/configuration)





All options live in `shared/sh-config.lua` (kept open when escrowed) and are commented inline.

## General [#general]

```lua
Config.Debug = false
Config.InteractionType = 'prompts'  -- 'target' (ox_target) or 'prompts' (sleepless_prompts)
Config.Minigames = 'tr_minigames'   -- 'builtin' (Config.Difficulty + eye_minigames) or 'tr_minigames'
Config.TrMinigames = {
    HotwireItem = 'wire_strippers', -- match Config.hotwire.item in tr_minigames
    HotwireCommand = 'hotwire',
}
Config.PromptPosition = 'bottom-center'

Config.DefaultKeybinds = { Lock = 'L', Ignition = 'G', Engine = 'M', Hotwire = 'H', Search = 'Y' }
Config.HoldingIgnitionWillToggleEngine = true
```

## Data & Key Cleanup [#data--key-cleanup]

```lua
Config.KeyCleanup = {
    Enabled = true,
    RemovedGraceSeconds = 5, -- wait after deletion, in case the vehicle respawns with the same plate
}
Config.VehicleDataRetentionMonths = 3
```

Keys for vehicles nobody owns are removed when the vehicle is deleted and after a server restart.
Player-owned vehicles always keep their keys.

## Keyfob & World Vehicles [#keyfob--world-vehicles]

```lua
Config.KeyfobDistance = 100.0
Config.AutoDriveDrivingFlag = 786603
Config.AutoDriveSpeed = 3.0

Config.JobKeys = true                   -- give keys for vehicles spawned by job scripts
Config.LockNPCVehicles = true
Config.LockParkedVehicles = true
Config.LockedVehiclesChance = 0.5
Config.DisableLeaveOnLockedDoors = true
```

## Hotwire, Lockpick & Search [#hotwire-lockpick--search]

```lua
Config.Hotwire = {
    Enabled = true,
    SaveHotwireState = true,          -- hotwire persists until the ignition is repaired
    Fixing = { Item = 'electrical_tools', SuccessDurabilityDecrease = 0.1, FailDurabilityDecrease = 0.25 },
    HotwireItem = 'electrical_tools', -- nil for no item
    SuccessDurabilityDecrease = 0.1,
    FailDurabilityDecrease = 0.25,
    AlarmChance = 0.6,
}

Config.Lockpick = {
    Enabled = true, Item = 'lockpick',
    SuccessDurabilityDecrease = 0.1, FailDurabilityDecrease = 0.25, AlarmChance = 0.6,
}

Config.AdvancedLockpick = {
    Enabled = true, Item = 'advanced_lockpick',
    SuccessDurabilityDecrease = 0.05, FailDurabilityDecrease = 0.1, AlarmChance = 0.3,
}

Config.KeySearching = { Enabled = true, Duration = 10, SearchingChance = 0.5 }
```

## Keyless System [#keyless-system]

```lua
Config.KeylessSystem = {
    Enabled = true,
    AutomaticallyDetectElectricModels = true,
    Models = { `neon` }, -- manual overrides
}
```

## Difficulty [#difficulty]

Used by the built-in flow. Lookup order: `ModelDifficulty` (by model name), then
`VehicleClassDifficulty` (by GTA class ID), then `DefaultDifficulty`.

```lua
Config.Difficulty = {
    DefaultDifficulty = 'medium',
    HotwireTimes   = { easy = 35000, medium = 28000, hard = 22000, expert = 18000 }, -- ms
    LockpickChance = { easy = 0.9, medium = 0.75, hard = 0.55, expert = 0.35 },
    AdvancedLockpickChance = { easy = 1.0, medium = 0.9, hard = 0.75, expert = 0.55 },
    HotwireChance  = { easy = 0.9, medium = 0.75, hard = 0.55, expert = 0.35 },
    MinigameLevel  = { easy = 1, medium = 2, hard = 3, expert = 4 },
    VehicleClassDifficulty = { [0] = 'easy', [7] = 'expert', --[[ ... ]] },
    ModelDifficulty = { ['adder'] = 'expert' },
}
```

<Callout type="info">
  Passing the minigame is not enough on its own: the server then rolls the tier's chance.
</Callout>

<details>
  <summary>
    GTA vehicle class IDs
  </summary>

  | ID | Class           | ID | Class       |
  | -- | --------------- | -- | ----------- |
  | 0  | Compacts        | 11 | Utility     |
  | 1  | Sedans          | 12 | Vans        |
  | 2  | SUVs            | 13 | Cycles      |
  | 3  | Coupes          | 14 | Boats       |
  | 4  | Muscle          | 15 | Helicopters |
  | 5  | Sports Classics | 16 | Planes      |
  | 6  | Sports          | 17 | Service     |
  | 7  | Super           | 18 | Emergency   |
  | 8  | Motorcycles     | 19 | Military    |
  | 9  | Off-road        | 20 | Commercial  |
  | 10 | Industrial      | 21 | Trains      |
</details>

## Blacklist [#blacklist]

```lua
Config.Blacklist = {
    Lockpick = true, -- set an action to false to allow it on blacklisted models
    Hotwire = true,
    Carjack = true,
    Models = { ['police'] = true, ['police2'] = true },
}
```

## Police Bypass [#police-bypass]

```lua
Config.PoliceBypass = {
    Enabled = true,
    RequireDuty = true,
    Jobs = { ['police'] = 0, ['sheriff'] = 0 }, -- job = minimum grade
    Item = 'police_bypass',                     -- nil = the job alone is enough
    UseItemToUnlock = true,                     -- using the item unlocks the closest vehicle
    Distance = 3.0,
}
```

## Dispatch [#dispatch]

```lua
Config.Dispatch = {
    Enabled = true,
    System = 'ps-dispatch', -- 'ps-dispatch' | 'builtin' | 'custom'
    Jobs = { 'police', 'sheriff' },
    Chance = { lockpick = 1.0, hotwire = 0.75, carjack = 1.0 },
    Blip = { sprite = 229, color = 1, scale = 1.0, time = 60 },
    Custom = function(data)
        -- data = { action, vehicle, plate, model, coords }
    end,
}
```

* **ps-dispatch** calls its `VehicleTheft` (lockpick, hotwire) or `CarJacking` alert.
* **builtin** sends a notification and a flashing blip to on-duty players in `Jobs`.
* **custom** runs `Custom(data)` on the offender's client, so you can call any dispatch export.

## Carjacking [#carjacking]

```lua
Config.Carjack = {
    Enabled = true,
    Duration = 6000,       -- progress bar (ms)
    Distance = 12.0,
    MaxSpeed = 15.0,       -- m/s
    SuccessChance = 0.85,
    FailBehavior = 'flee', -- 'flee' or 'fight'
    Cooldown = 30,         -- seconds per player
    GiveKeys = true,
    MeleeAllowed = false,
}
```

## Locksmith [#locksmith]

```lua
Config.Locksmith = {
    Job = 'locksmith',
    RequireDuty = true,
    Items = {
        OBD            = { item = 'locksmith_tablet', degrade = 0.1 },
        KeyCuttingTool = { item = 'key_cutting_tool', degrade = 0.1 },
        BlankKey       = { item = 'blank_key' },
    },
    Interactions = {
        { coords = vec3(165.660, -1810.262, 29.275), type = 'KeyCutting' },
    },
    Blips = {
        { coords = vec3(167.32, -1803.38, 29.32), label = 'Locksmith', sprite = 811, color = 5, scale = 1.0 },
    },
    OfflineStore = {
        Enabled = true,
        MininumDuty = 0, -- NPC store opens when on-duty locksmiths <= this
        Prices = { Mechanical = 1000, Wireless = 5000 },
        Locations = {
            {
                coords = vec4(165.55, -1808.37, 28.32, 320.84),
                anim = { dict = 'anim@amb@nightclub@lazlow@ig1_vip@', name = 'clubvip_base_laz', flag = 1 },
                model = `s_m_y_xmech_01`,
            },
        },
    },
}
```


# Exports (/docs/paid_resources/filo_vehiclekeys/exports)





## Server [#server]

`target` can be a plate, network ID or entity.

```lua
exports.filo_vehiclekeys:GiveKeys(source, target, forceGive, invalidateOldKey)
exports.filo_vehiclekeys:RemoveKeys(source, target)
exports.filo_vehiclekeys:GiveJobKeys(plate, job)
exports.filo_vehiclekeys:RemoveJobKeys(plate, job)
exports.filo_vehiclekeys:SetKeysInIgnition(plate, keysInIgnition, canRemove)
exports.filo_vehiclekeys:SetLockState(vehicle, locked) -- boolean, or 2 = locked / 1 = unlocked
exports.filo_vehiclekeys:HasVehicleAccess(source, vehicle) -- keys, job keys or police bypass
```

## Client [#client]

```lua
exports.filo_vehiclekeys:GiveKeys(vehicle, invalidateOldKey)
exports.filo_vehiclekeys:GiveKeysByPlate(plate, invalidateOldKey)
exports.filo_vehiclekeys:RemoveKeys(vehicle)
exports.filo_vehiclekeys:RemoveKeysByPlate(plate)

exports.filo_vehiclekeys:HasKeys(vehicle)
exports.filo_vehiclekeys:HasKeysByPlate(plate)
exports.filo_vehiclekeys:HasJobKeys(vehicle)
exports.filo_vehiclekeys:HasJobKeysByPlate(plate)
exports.filo_vehiclekeys:HasVehicleAccess(vehicle) -- keys, job keys or police bypass
exports.filo_vehiclekeys:HasPoliceBypass()

exports.filo_vehiclekeys:GiveJobKeys(vehicle, job)
exports.filo_vehiclekeys:RemoveJobKeys(vehicle, job)
exports.filo_vehiclekeys:SetKeysInIgnition(plate, keysInIgnition, canRemove)
```

<Callout type="info">
  `StartEngineWithoutKeys` is also exported for tr\_core's key bridge. You don't need to call it yourself.
</Callout>


# Flows (/docs/paid_resources/filo_vehiclekeys/flows)





## Lockpicking & Hotwiring [#lockpicking--hotwiring]

Every attempt resolves to a difficulty tier (`easy` / `medium` / `hard` / `expert`) from
`ModelDifficulty`, then `VehicleClassDifficulty`, then `DefaultDifficulty`.

* **Lockpick:** use `lockpick` or `advanced_lockpick` near a locked vehicle. Pass the minigame, then the server rolls the tier's chance. Tools lose durability and may trigger the alarm.
* **Hotwire:** press `H` in a vehicle you have no key for, with `Config.Hotwire.HotwireItem`. A progress bar runs for the tier's time, then the minigame at the tier's level, then the server rolls the chance.
* **Search:** press `Y` in a parked vehicle to search for its key (`Config.KeySearching`).

Models in `Config.Blacklist.Models` can't be lockpicked, hotwired or carjacked (per action).

<Callout type="info">
  With `Config.Minigames = 'tr_minigames'`, tr\_minigames handles these flows. See
  [Compatibility](/docs/paid_resources/filo_vehiclekeys/compatibility#tr_minigames).
</Callout>

## Carjacking [#carjacking]

Aim a gun at an NPC driver within `Distance` of a car slower than `MaxSpeed`. The driver brakes and
a progress bar starts; it cancels if you stop aiming or move away.

* **Success:** the driver gets out and runs, the car unlocks, you get its key and police are alerted.
* **Failure:** the driver drives off or fights back (`FailBehavior`).

The aim check only runs while a weapon is drawn. Each player has a `Cooldown` between attempts.

## Police [#police]

Jobs in `Config.PoliceBypass.Jobs` (at the minimum grade, on duty, and carrying `police_bypass` if
set) can lock, unlock, insert the ignition and start the engine on any vehicle. With
`UseItemToUnlock`, using the item unlocks the closest vehicle. Carjacking a blacklisted vehicle
with the bypass is allowed and sends no dispatch.

Successful lockpicks, hotwires and carjacks send a dispatch alert based on `Config.Dispatch.Chance`.

## Locksmith [#locksmith]

* **Key cutting:** at a key cutting station or with the `key_cutting_tool`. Copies a key from the locksmith's inventory or a nearby vehicle. Uses a `blank_key`.
* **OBD programming:** for keyless vehicles. The locksmith sits in the driver's seat and uses the `locksmith_tablet`.
* **Invalidate old keys:** optional when making a key. Generates a new key ID so every old copy stops working.
* **NPC store:** when `OfflineStore.MininumDuty` or fewer locksmiths are on duty, players can buy spare keys for vehicles they own. Prices are enforced on the server.
* **Ignition repair:** use `electrical_tools` in a hotwired vehicle to clear the hotwire. Only needed when `Config.Hotwire.SaveHotwireState` is on.

## Admin Panel [#admin-panel]

`/keyadmin` lists stored and spawned vehicles (spawned ones have a green dot). For each vehicle you can:

* toggle keyless, keys-in-ignition, engine-on and hotwired
* add or remove jobs with access
* regenerate the key ID, making every existing key useless
* give a key to an online player
* delete the stored record

Every action is checked on the server against the `command.keyadmin` permission.

## Key Validation [#key-validation]

A key item is valid when its plate and key ID match the vehicle's current key ID. The server keeps
that ID on the spawned vehicle, or in the `filo_vehiclekeys` table for owned vehicles that aren't
spawned. Checks never trust client data.

Keys for unowned vehicles (NPC, stolen or job cars) are removed when the vehicle is deleted and
after a server restart (`Config.KeyCleanup`). Player-owned vehicles always keep their keys.


# 🔑 filo_vehiclekeys (/docs/paid_resources/filo_vehiclekeys)





[![Buy on Tebex](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tebex-blue?style=for-the-badge\&logo=tebex)](https://filo.tebex.io/package/filo-vehiclekeys)

Item-based vehicle keys for FiveM: physical keys and key fobs, ignition handling, lockpicking,
hotwiring, NPC carjacking, a locksmith job, police dispatch and an admin panel. All outcomes are
decided on the server and everything is tuned from `shared/sh-config.lua`.

<Callout type="info">
  Current version: **2.0.0**. Framework, inventory, minigame, dispatch and target code lives in the
  open `bridge/` folder, so you can adapt it to your server.
</Callout>

## Features [#features]

**Keys**

* Keys are `vehiclekey` items tied to a plate and a key ID; a new key ID instantly invalidates every old copy
* Mechanical keys and keyless fobs (auto-detected for electric models, or per model)
* Key fob UI: lock, unlock, trunk, panic, remote engine, convertible roof, summon, auto-lock and auto-start
* Insert/remove keys from the ignition, hold to start the engine
* Job keys: give a whole job access to a vehicle without an item
* Keys for unowned vehicles are removed on despawn and after a restart

**Theft**

* Lockpick and advanced lockpick with per-tier success chances, durability and alarm chance
* Hotwiring with per-tier times and minigame difficulty
* Difficulty tiers mapped by GTA vehicle class, with per-model overrides
* Searching parked vehicles for keys
* NPC carjacking: aim at a driver, hold them up, take the car and its key
* Model blacklist per action

**Police**

* Bypass for configured jobs (grade, duty, optional `police_bypass` item)
* Dispatch alerts via ps-dispatch, a built-in notify + blip, or your own function

**Locksmith & Admin**

* Key cutting, OBD fob programming and ignition repair
* NPC store for spare keys when not enough locksmiths are on duty
* `/keyadmin` panel to manage vehicles, key IDs, job access and keys

# Installation (/docs/paid_resources/filo_vehiclekeys/installation)





## Dependencies [#dependencies]

| Resource                                                                         | Required    | Used for                                                                                          |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [ox\_lib](https://github.com/overextended/ox_lib)                                | Yes         | Callbacks, keybinds, progress bars, notifications                                                 |
| [oxmysql](https://github.com/overextended/oxmysql)                               | Yes         | Key data storage                                                                                  |
| [community\_bridge](https://github.com/blamefilo/community_bridge)               | Yes         | Framework, inventory and notification bridge                                                      |
| [sleepless\_prompts](https://github.com/Sleepless-Development/sleepless_prompts) | Yes         | In-vehicle and locksmith prompts (included in the download)                                       |
| [eye\_minigames](https://github.com/invalid0190/eye_minigames)                   | Default     | Minigames when `Config.Minigames = 'builtin'`                                                     |
| tr\_minigames + tr\_core                                                         | Optional    | Physical lockpick and hotwire when `Config.Minigames = 'tr_minigames'` (included, pre-configured) |
| ox\_target                                                                       | Optional    | Locksmith interactions when `Config.InteractionType = 'target'`                                   |
| ps-dispatch                                                                      | Optional    | Dispatch when `Config.Dispatch.System = 'ps-dispatch'`                                            |
| [xsound](https://github.com/Xogy/xsound)                                         | Optional    | Ignition sounds                                                                                   |
| filo\_blips                                                                      | Optional    | Locksmith blips (falls back to native blips)                                                      |
| baseevents                                                                       | Recommended | Lock state and NPC vehicle locking on entry                                                       |

Supported frameworks (through community\_bridge): Qbox, QBCore and ESX.

<Callout type="warn">
  `filo_textui` is no longer used. v2.0.0 uses `sleepless_prompts` for all prompts.
</Callout>

## Setup [#setup]

<Steps>
  <Step>
    Put 

    `filo_vehiclekeys`

     (and 

    `sleepless_prompts`

    , 

    `tr_core`

    , 

    `tr_minigames`

     from the download) in your resources folder.
  </Step>

  <Step>
    Add the items from 

    `INSTALL/ox_inventory.txt`

     to your inventory and copy the images from 

    `INSTALL/item images`

    . If you use tr_minigames, also add 

    `wire_strippers`

     from 

    `tr_minigames/install/ox_inventory/items.lua`

    .
  </Step>

  <Step>
    Ensure the resources after their dependencies:

    ```
    ensure ox_lib
    ensure oxmysql
    ensure community_bridge
    ensure sleepless_prompts
    ensure filo_vehiclekeys
    ensure tr_core      # only with Config.Minigames = 'tr_minigames'
    ensure tr_minigames
    ```
  </Step>

  <Step>
    Start the server. The 

    `filo_vehiclekeys`

     table is created automatically.
  </Step>

  <Step>
    Remove any other vehicle key resource. This one provides 

    `qb-vehiclekeys`

    , 

    `qbx_vehiclekeys`

     and 

    `filo_vehiclekey`

    .
  </Step>
</Steps>

## Items [#items]

| Item                             | Purpose                                                       |
| -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `vehiclekey`                     | The key or fob itself (metadata holds plate and key ID)       |
| `lockpick` / `advanced_lockpick` | Lockpicking                                                   |
| `electrical_tools`               | Hotwiring and repairing hotwired ignitions                    |
| `blank_key`                      | Consumed when a locksmith makes a key                         |
| `key_cutting_tool`               | Cutting mechanical keys                                       |
| `locksmith_tablet`               | Programming fobs over OBD                                     |
| `police_bypass`                  | Police master key (only if `Config.PoliceBypass.Item` is set) |

```lua
["police_bypass"] = {
    label = "Police Master Key",
    weight = 50,
    stack = false,
    close = true,
    description = "Unlocks and starts any vehicle (police only).",
},
```

<Callout type="info">
  `vehiclekey` must have `stack = false`: each key is a unique item with its own metadata.
</Callout>

## Controls [#controls]

| Default key | Action                                             |
| ----------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `L`         | Lock / unlock the closest vehicle                  |
| `G`         | Insert / remove the key (hold to start the engine) |
| `M`         | Engine on / off                                    |
| `H`         | Hotwire                                            |
| `Y`         | Search the vehicle for keys                        |

Players can rebind these in the FiveM key bindings menu. Defaults are in `Config.DefaultKeybinds`.

## Commands [#commands]

| Command                                     | Permission    | Description                                                                                                      |
| ------------------------------------------- | ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `/givekey [id] [plate]` (alias `/givekeys`) | `group.admin` | Give a key. Defaults to yourself and your current vehicle. Plates may contain spaces. Works for stored vehicles. |
| `/givejobkey <job> [plate]`                 | `group.admin` | Give a job access to a spawned vehicle                                                                           |
| `/keyadmin`                                 | `group.admin` | Open the admin panel                                                                                             |

## SQL Table [#sql-table]

Created automatically on first boot. Only player-owned vehicles are written, and records
inactive for `Config.VehicleDataRetentionMonths` are pruned.

```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS `filo_vehiclekeys` (
    `plate`      VARCHAR(15) NOT NULL,
    `data`       LONGTEXT    NOT NULL,
    `updated_at` TIMESTAMP   NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
                              ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    PRIMARY KEY (`plate`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;
```
